tasks.short: Interview new patients and complete admission forms

steps.what: Verify the new patient's identity and read the available admission information
Interview the patient about mental health, current needs and treatment history
Complete admission forms with the patient's actual account and verified details
Check the admission history for accuracy, uncertainty and concerns requiring clinical attention
Save the completed admission forms in the existing care record

tasks.design: Configure the existing admission form in the care-record tool {OTHER} to reuse verified demographic fields and consistent history headings. The technician conducts the interview, records the actual account and checks uncertainty and clinical concerns; no model infers mental health status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated demographic entry and form layout interrupt the real admission interview and write-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record-linked admission forms can reuse factual fields without replacing clinical questioning.
tasks.still_hard: Distress, incomplete recall and conflicting accounts require careful listening and clinical escalation through the existing pathway.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and distinguish observed facts, the patient's report and uncertainty.

ambition.what: Admission interviewing and recognition of concerns remain human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native admission forms can reuse verified demographics while mental-health interviewing and factual history checking remain clinical work.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing patient care-record tool and interview setting. Boundary is the interview and its actual admission forms, not diagnosis, treatment orders or an invented later report.

The referring service and registration team supply the existing record; the technician verifies identity and details in s1. The patient supplies history in s2, and the technician captures and checks it in s3 and s4. Missing facts stay unknown or are manually obtained within retained work.

s3 removes six units of repeated verified demographic fields and form headings, retaining19 for actual history and observations. No recording or automated history extraction is introduced. Native reuse already active earns no saving.

Ordinary same-record author save is one fully retained unit with no gate or self-approval. Existing urgent clinical escalation remains required if concerns arise; it is not claimed as an automated action or saving.
unknowns: Which admission fields are currently re-entered
research_questions: Can the form preserve conflicting accounts without silently overwriting them with referral data?

incremental.description: Maintain admission fields and correct unsuitable demographic mappings

tasks.design: Use native availability comparison in {CALENDAR} and reusable conference fields in the existing secure care-communication tool {OTHER}. The technician checks the permitted contact route and talks with relatives; the actual conference organiser checks the complete arrangement before reservation and confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual calendar comparison and repeated conference fields surround a sensitive scheduling call.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendar comparison and a factual confirmation form remove clerical work without replacing the relative conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Permission to contact, family relationships and access needs need individual attention.
tasks.human_edge: Arrange a respectful and workable conference without disclosing unnecessary health information.

ambition.what: The technician retains sensitive contact and conference coordination.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native calendars can compare availability, while sensitive family contact and confirmation checks remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing patient contact-permission record and secure care messaging tool. Boundary includes actual calendar reservation and the existing written confirmation, not a new clinical case summary.

The care team maintains permitted contacts and the conference request; calendar owners maintain availability. The technician verifies them in s1 and captures relatives' availability and access details in s4 after the call. No missing permission or calendar data is inferred.

s2 replaces actual manual comparison of the required clinical calendars. Missing calendar access requires funded manual repair. s4 removes three units of repeated participant and venue fields, retaining12 for the actual agreement, contact checks and corrections.

The scenario uses the existing clinical conference organiser's final arrangement check, not an author approving personal notes. s5 checks the exact proposal and confirmation after they exist; edits invalidate both actions. The operative reservation and real send each have their own gate and remain at their current small time. Ordinary draft saving has no gate or saving.
Relative participation is unchanged and outside this technician-labour boundary. No patient self-service work is substituted free. Existing native functions already used earn no additional benefit.
unknowns: Actual conference organiser and contact permissions
research_questions: Can the final confirmation avoid unnecessary patient details while preserving the agreed arrangement?

Exact conference confirmation and permitted recipient destination checked in s5; edits void authority
